articles.title: Google patches Chrome zero-day exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-11645)
articles.summary: Google has released an urgent update for Chrome to patch a high-severity, actively exploited zero-day vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-11645. The fix is currently rolling out across Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms.

articles.title: Apple Intelligence can now replace weak passwords without user intervention
articles.summary: Apple is enhancing its Passwords app by integrating Apple Intelligence to automatically identify and replace weak, reused, or compromised passwords. This feature streamlines security management by reducing manual user intervention for credential updates.

articles.title: French govt messaging service breached in account hijacking attack
articles.summary: The French government's encrypted messaging platform, Tchap, was breached after hackers compromised a legitimate user account to gain unauthorized access. DINUM confirmed the incident and warned users following the security lapse.

articles.title: Google fixes the fifth actively exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026
articles.summary: Google has released an emergency patch for CVE-2026-11645, a critical zero-day vulnerability in the Chrome V8 engine that is currently being exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Handala Claims Israeli Radar Hack, But Evidence Shows Phone Admin Panel
articles.summary: The hacker group Handala claimed a significant cyberattack against Israeli radar systems, but investigation revealed the evidence actually displayed a simple administrative panel for a mobile device. This suggests the group is employing misleading claims for psychological impact rather than executing a high-level military breach.

articles.title: New FROST Attack Lets Websites Track What Sites and Apps You Open via SSD Timing
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a side-channel attack called FROST that uses SSD timing and JavaScript to track a user's browsing activity and opened applications without requiring special permissions. The attack exploits storage contention to monitor system activity stealthily.

articles.title: Mythos Preview can weaponize N-day vulnerabilities in hours
articles.summary: Anthropic research reveals that the Mythos Preview AI tool can weaponize disclosed N-day vulnerabilities within hours, significantly accelerating the threat window for unpatched systems. This capability highlights the heightened danger posed by existing vulnerabilities that remain unpatched after disclosure.

articles.title: Qilin NHS breach tally grows as Essex trust confirms stolen records
articles.summary: The Qilin ransomware attack on the NHS continues to impact patients two years later as the Essex Partnership University Trust confirms additional records were stolen. Authorities are currently working to identify and notify affected individuals.

articles.title: Hades PyPI Attack: 19 Packages Poisoned to Auto-Run Bun Credential Stealer
articles.summary: The Hades supply chain attack involves 19 malicious PyPI packages that utilize a *-setup.pth file to automatically execute a credential-stealing payload. This campaign is part of the ongoing Miasma series targeting Python developers.

articles.title: CISA gives feds 3 days to patch Check Point VPN bug exploited as zero-day
articles.summary: CISA has issued an emergency directive requiring U.S. federal agencies to patch a critical Check Point VPN vulnerability within three days due to its exploitation by Qilin ransomware affiliates. This action aims to secure government networks against active zero-day attacks targeting remote access infrastructure.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds BerriAI LiteLLM and Check Point Security Gateway flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added critical vulnerabilities identified in BerriAI LiteLLM and Check Point Security Gateway to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring immediate attention from federal agencies and affected organizations.

articles.title: CVE-2026-23111: Linux nf_tables Flaw Enables Root Exploits
articles.summary: A critical use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's nf_tables framework allows local users to achieve privilege escalation to root. The flaw was identified by Exodus Intelligence researcher Oliver Sieber and stems from a minor logic error.

articles.title: Google patches new Chrome zero-day flaw exploited in the wild
articles.summary: Google has issued an emergency update for Chrome to address the fifth zero-day vulnerability exploited in the wild this year. Users are urged to update their browsers immediately to mitigate potential security risks.

articles.title: LiteLLM Flaw CVE-2026-42271 Exploited in the Wild, Chains to Unauthenticated RCE
articles.summary: CISA has added the high-severity command injection vulnerability CVE-2026-42271 in BerriAI LiteLLM to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to reports of active in-the-wild exploitation. This flaw allows authenticated users to execute arbitrary commands, posing a significant risk to affected systems.

articles.title: The architecture of subtraction: Why it’s time to erase the roads, not just map the traffic
articles.summary: The article argues that reactive patching is no longer sufficient against AI-driven threats and suggests a shift toward an 'architecture of subtraction' to eliminate vulnerabilities entirely. This approach focuses on reducing attack surfaces by removing unnecessary complexity rather than just addressing known security flaws.

articles.title: Treating AI agents like service accounts for federated query security
articles.summary: The article discusses Starburst's approach to data governance in federated query environments, specifically focusing on treating AI agents as service accounts to secure autonomous data access. It highlights strategies for managing access controls, audit trails, and mitigating prompt injection risks in AI-driven SQL generation.

articles.title: Malware ships with bugs that defenders could use against it
articles.summary: Researchers analyzing leaked malware samples found that approximately 90 percent of the projects contain exploitable software vulnerabilities that defenders could potentially leverage. This highlights that malicious code often suffers from the same quality control issues as legitimate software.

articles.title: The security questions around Chinese AI coding models in U.S. software
articles.summary: Booz Allen Hamilton research indicates that U.S. developers using Chinese-made AI coding models face significant security risks, particularly regarding potential data exposure and supply chain vulnerabilities. The testing revealed that these models may behave differently when prompted with government-related contexts, raising concerns about the integrity of U.S. software.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: June 9, 2026
articles.summary: Help Net Security provides a curated list of current job openings in the cybersecurity field for June 9, 2026, featuring roles such as Application Security Architect and Application Security Engineer.

articles.title: When “Hi, This Is IT” Comes Through Microsoft Teams
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are increasingly exploiting Microsoft Teams to conduct social engineering attacks by masquerading as IT support. Organizations are advised to implement security best practices to mitigate the risks associated with these collaboration platform threats.

articles.title: WhatsApp Says It Blocked Pegasus Spyware Campaign Linked to NSO
articles.summary: WhatsApp has successfully blocked a surveillance campaign orchestrated by the NSO Group using its Pegasus spyware and is seeking legal action in a U.S. court for a breach of injunction. This move highlights an ongoing legal and technical battle against the deployment of sophisticated commercial spyware targeting mobile users.

articles.title: Norks blast 250+ fake job offers to developers over 6 weeks to try and snarf creds and crypto
articles.summary: North Korean state-sponsored actors have launched a campaign using over 250 fraudulent job offers to target software developers, aiming to steal credentials and cryptocurrency. The operation reflects an ongoing effort to exploit technical professionals for financial gain.

articles.title: NFCShare Android malware spreads via fake banking app updates on GitHub
articles.summary: The NFCShare Android malware is actively targeting users by masquerading as legitimate banking app updates hosted on GitHub. This campaign leverages social engineering to infect devices through third-party distribution platforms.

articles.title: SoFi confirms third-party data breach at Hong Kong subsidiary
articles.summary: SoFi Hong Kong reported a data breach caused by unauthorized access to a database held by a third-party vendor. The incident exposed customer information to external attackers.

articles.title: New Apple feature automatically changes your compromised passwords
articles.summary: Apple introduced an AI-powered feature for Safari in iOS 27 that automatically updates weak or compromised user passwords. This capability aims to improve account security by proactively addressing credential vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Meta Accuses NSO of Violating WhatsApp Court Injunction
articles.summary: Meta has accused NSO Group of breaching a permanent court injunction by continuing to target WhatsApp users with phishing campaigns and unauthorized test accounts. This legal escalation follows a previous landmark ruling that explicitly prohibited NSO Group from accessing or targeting Meta's platforms.

articles.title: New Shai-Hulud attack trojanizes 19 science-focused PyPI packages
articles.summary: Hackers have compromised 19 science-focused PyPI packages in a supply-chain attack dubbed Shai-Hulud, which aims to steal sensitive secrets from developers. The malicious packages have been downloaded hundreds of thousands of times, posing a significant risk to the software supply chain.

articles.title: UK gives big tech 3 months to create device controls to block nude images of kids
articles.summary: The UK government has mandated that tech companies implement device-level controls within three months to detect and block nude imagery of minors on smartphones and tablets. This regulatory measure aims to enhance online child safety through mandatory technical solutions.

articles.title: One-Character Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Local Root Access, Exploits Now Public
articles.summary: A critical use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's nf_tables component allows local unprivileged users to gain root access and escape containers. Publicly available exploit code increases the risk of exploitation for unpatched systems.

articles.title: Operation FlutterBridge Uses Fake Google Ads to Spread macOS Backdoor
articles.summary: Operation FlutterBridge employs malicious Google advertisements and shell companies to distribute a new macOS backdoor known as FlutterShell. The campaign leverages these deceptive tactics to compromise unsuspecting users' systems.

articles.title: WhatsApp says it disrupted new NSO spyware phishing attacks
articles.summary: WhatsApp successfully identified and blocked spear-phishing campaigns attributed to the NSO Group following reports of targeted social engineering. The intervention prevented potential exploitation of users by the controversial spyware developer.

articles.title: Meta claims NSO Group still targets WhatsApp users despite court order
articles.summary: Meta has accused NSO Group of violating a court injunction by continuing to target WhatsApp users through spear-phishing attacks. The company is seeking to have the spyware vendor held in contempt of court.

articles.title: Meta accuses NSO Group of defying spyware injunction, files contempt of court complaint
articles.summary: Meta has filed a contempt of court complaint against NSO Group, alleging the firm violated a previous injunction by launching spearphishing campaigns against WhatsApp users. This legal action highlights ongoing efforts to hold the spyware developer accountable for unauthorized surveillance activities.

articles.title: Ransomware crims got a month-long head start on Check Point VPN 0-day that now has a fix
articles.summary: Threat actors, including a Qilin ransomware affiliate, exploited a Check Point VPN zero-day vulnerability for a month before a patch was released. The flaw allowed unauthorized access, and users are urged to apply the available fix immediately.

articles.title: Armenia’s pro-Europe party wins election despite Russia-linked disinformation
articles.summary: Armenia's pro-Europe Civil Contract party secured a significant electoral victory despite encountering an influence campaign linked to Russian-aligned actors. The result highlights the ongoing role of disinformation in geopolitical elections.

articles.title: Meta Blocks NSO Group's New WhatsApp Phishing Attack, Files Contempt Order
articles.summary: Meta has blocked NSO Group spear-phishing attempts targeting WhatsApp users and is seeking a federal court contempt order for violating a permanent injunction. The legal action alleges that NSO Group bypassed previous restrictions to conduct malicious activity.

articles.title: Hackers Clone Ghidra, dnSpy and Other Tool Sites to Spread Malware
articles.summary: Threat actors are creating fraudulent websites mimicking popular reverse-engineering tools like Ghidra and dnSpy to distribute malware such as RemusStealer and various loaders. Users are tricked into downloading malicious binaries instead of the legitimate software.

articles.title: WhatsApp says NSO targeted users with spearfishing attacks in violation of court order
articles.summary: WhatsApp has filed a motion for a contempt order against NSO Group, alleging that the company violated a court injunction by continuing to target users with spear-phishing attacks.

articles.title: Microsoft changes how Defender for Endpoint EDR updates are delivered on Windows
articles.summary: Microsoft is transitioning Defender for Endpoint EDR updates to be delivered independently of monthly Windows OS updates via Microsoft Update. This change aims to accelerate the deployment of security improvements across Windows 10 and 11 devices by fall 2026.

articles.title: Gogs patches critical zero-day enabling remote code execution
articles.summary: Gogs has released a patch for a critical zero-day vulnerability that could allow attackers to execute remote code and gain unauthorized access to private repositories. Users of internet-facing instances are advised to update immediately to mitigate the risk of compromise.

articles.title: Critical UniFi OS bug lets hackers gain root without authentication
articles.summary: A chain of three previously disclosed vulnerabilities in Ubiquiti UniFi OS allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution with root-level access. Although patches are available, the flaw poses a significant risk to systems that remain unupdated.

articles.title: Ransomware sends Illinois high school on an early summer vacation
articles.summary: An Illinois high school was forced to close early due to a ransomware attack, while a separate cyberattack impacted 13 schools across Wales. Both incidents highlight the increasing vulnerability of educational institutions to disruptive malware campaigns.

articles.title: Critical Check Point VPN Flaw Exploited to Bypass Passwords in IKEv1 Setups
articles.summary: Check Point has reported active exploitation of a critical, high-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-50751) in its VPN products that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass password authentication via IKEv1. Users are urged to address deployments using this deprecated key exchange protocol.

articles.title: Everest Forms Pro WordPress Flaw is Handing Attackers Admin Access
articles.summary: Service busy.

articles.title: Russia upgrades rules for its digital spy system to better track citizens online
articles.summary: Russia has updated the technical standards for its SORM surveillance system, enhancing the government's ability to monitor and track citizens' online activities. These new regulations formalize stricter control over digital communications data.

articles.title: Reducing security operations complexity with Wazuh Cloud
articles.summary: Wazuh Cloud aims to alleviate security operations challenges like alert fatigue and infrastructure maintenance by offering a managed, scalable SIEM/XDR platform with AI-driven analysis. This solution helps teams streamline their workflows within complex hybrid environments.

articles.title: GitHub nukes 70+ Microsoft repos, breaks CI/CD pipelines, following suspected worm infections
articles.summary: GitHub suspended over 70 Microsoft repositories after they were compromised by the Miasma worm, which aimed to scrape cloud secrets. The removal caused widespread disruption to CI/CD pipelines relying on those repositories.

articles.title: Hackers used Meta’s AI support system to hijack over 20,000 Instagram accounts
articles.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Meta's AI-assisted 'High Touch Support' recovery system to hijack over 20,000 Instagram accounts by triggering unauthorized password resets. The flaw allowed unauthorized parties to bypass standard security measures within the account recovery workflow.

articles.title: Silent Ransom Group Uses Fast Flux Botnet to Hide Law Firm Leak Sites
articles.summary: The Silent Ransom Group is targeting law firms through data theft and vishing, leveraging fast flux botnet technology to obfuscate their leak sites. This tactic aims to make their malicious infrastructure harder to track and take down.

articles.title: New Relic expands observability into AI-assisted software development
articles.summary: New Relic has launched an open-source AI Coding Observability tool designed to provide visibility and auditing capabilities for AI-assisted software development workflows. This tool addresses the visibility gaps created when organizations integrate AI coding assistants into their existing development environments.

articles.title: AI Phishing Is Crushing SOCs with Alert Volume: How to Reduce Tier 1 Overload
articles.summary: The use of AI-generated phishing content is significantly increasing the volume of security alerts, overwhelming Tier 1 SOC analysts and creating a risk of missing actual threats. Organizations must adopt strategies to manage this alert surge to prevent critical credential theft or malware incidents.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Instagram Account Hacks, Android Zero-Day, GitHub Worm and More
articles.summary: This weekly recap highlights a series of cyber threats including Instagram account compromises, an Android zero-day, and a malicious worm spreading through GitHub repositories. The report emphasizes that despite sophisticated threats, many incidents continue to stem from basic security oversights and ongoing unauthorized inbox access.

articles.title: Check Point links VPN zero-day attacks to Qilin ransomware gang
articles.summary: Check Point has patched a critical zero-day vulnerability in its VPN products that was actively exploited by the Qilin ransomware group. The company issued security updates to address the flaw and protect impacted Remote Access and Mobile Access deployments.

articles.title: Qilin ransomware affiliate exploited Check Point VPN zero-day (CVE-2026-50751)
articles.summary: A Qilin ransomware affiliate is actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-50751) affecting Check Point's Remote Access and Mobile Access VPN solutions. Users are urged to address the flaw to prevent unauthorized network access.

articles.title: NSO Group back in Meta's crosshairs after alleged WhatsApp targeting
articles.summary: Meta has renewed legal action against NSO Group, alleging that the surveillance firm continued to conduct phishing operations against WhatsApp users despite previous court injunctions. This development highlights ongoing friction between tech platforms and spyware vendors regarding the misuse of communication services.

articles.title: The Hardest Fork
articles.summary: A security researcher claims that a complex, novel chain of minor vulnerabilities dubbed 'Mythos' poses a significant, credible threat, countering industry skepticism that it is merely a marketing stunt.

articles.title: RidgeBot 7.0 automates Active Directory attack simulations for security validation
articles.summary: Ridge Security has released RidgeBot 7.0, a security platform update that automates Active Directory penetration testing to identify and simulate potential domain compromise risks. This tool allows security teams to validate defenses against tactics like credential extraction and lateral movement.

articles.title: Instagram Recovery Tool Bug Exposed 20,225 Accounts to Password Reset Abuse
articles.summary: A vulnerability in an Instagram recovery tool allowed unauthorized password resets, potentially exposing 20,225 accounts to takeover attempts. Users without two-factor authentication were particularly susceptible to this exploit.

articles.title: ConnectSecure’s Patch 360 gives MSPs control over patch testing and deployment
articles.summary: ConnectSecure has launched Patch 360, a patch management platform designed for MSPs that features a test-and-trust framework to validate patches before widespread deployment. The tool aims to reduce operational risk by providing visibility throughout the entire remediation lifecycle, from pilot testing to potential rollback.

articles.title: Oxford University discloses data breach after careers platform hack
articles.summary: Oxford University reported a data breach affecting its CareerConnect platform following a security incident at its third-party provider, Group GTI.

articles.title: UNC3753 Escalates: From Vishing Calls to Physical Office Intrusions at US Legal and Financial Firms
articles.summary: The cybercrime group UNC3753 is intensifying its extortion campaign by combining vishing-based remote access attacks with physical office intrusions to compromise sensitive data. This evolution demonstrates a hybrid approach where attackers use social engineering to gain digital access and physical presence to deploy malicious hardware.

articles.title: VerdantBamboo Deploys BSD Variant of BRICKSTORM on Linux Appliances
articles.summary: The cyber espionage group VerdantBamboo, linked to Clay Typhoon, is targeting Linux appliances with a BSD variant of the BRICKSTORM backdoor alongside two other malware families. This campaign demonstrates an evolving strategy to compromise Linux-based infrastructure.

articles.title: CISA: Patch actively exploited SolarWinds Serv-U DoS vulnerability (CVE-2026-28318)
articles.summary: CISA has issued an emergency directive for federal agencies to patch or mitigate an actively exploited uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in SolarWinds Serv-U that allows for remote denial-of-service attacks.

articles.title: Instagram Glitch Reportedly Exposed Contact Info of Zuckerberg and Other Users
articles.summary: An Instagram password reset flaw exposed the private contact information, including email addresses and phone numbers, of high-profile users such as Mark Zuckerberg. The incident highlights a significant vulnerability in the platform's account recovery process.

articles.title: The AI security race needs accountability, not overregulation
articles.summary: The article argues that the AI security industry should prioritize industry accountability and collaborative partnerships over strict government-mandated regulations to foster responsible innovation. It suggests that voluntary cooperation between policymakers and technology firms is a more effective strategy for managing AI security risks.

articles.title: Meta AI Recovery Tool Flaw Exposed 20,000+ Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: A vulnerability in Meta's High Touch Support tool allowed unauthorized individuals to reset passwords and hijack over 20,000 Instagram accounts.

articles.title: Samsung just made Galaxy phones more secure in One UI 9 beta
articles.summary: Samsung has integrated a new 'Lockdown mode' into the One UI 9 beta power menu, which disables biometric authentication and forces a PIN or password for device access. This update enhances device security by preventing unauthorized access through biometric bypass.

articles.title: OpenAI is locking down parts of ChatGPT to reduce data theft risks
articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced a new 'Lockdown Mode' for ChatGPT to help users mitigate data exfiltration and prompt injection risks by restricting access to external resources. This optional security feature is available across various personal and business subscription plans.

articles.title: UNC3753 Used Vishing and Physical Intrusions in U.S. Data Theft Extortion Campaign
articles.summary: The threat actor UNC3753 is targeting U.S. professional and financial services through a campaign involving vishing and physical intrusions to facilitate data theft and extortion. The activity, observed between January and May 2026, has been attributed by Google Mandiant and GTIG.

articles.title: IoT Botnet C0XMO Adds Competitor-Killing Capability
articles.summary: The newly identified Gafgyt botnet variant, C0XMO, exploits historical router vulnerabilities to hijack IoT devices, eliminate competing malware, and facilitate large-scale DDoS attacks.

articles.title: VS Code Adds 2-Hour Extension Auto-Update Delay to Limit Supply Chain Attacks
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing a two-hour delay for automatic Visual Studio Code extension updates to mitigate the risk of malicious code injection via supply chain attacks. This brief buffer allows for potential threats to be detected and mitigated before updates are widely distributed.

articles.title: Over 20,000 Instagram accounts stolen in Meta AI support hack
articles.summary: Attackers exploited Meta's AI-powered support system to compromise over 20,000 Instagram accounts by triggering unauthorized password resets. This incident highlights a significant security flaw in automated account recovery processes.

articles.title: DockSec: Open-source AI-powered Docker security scanner
articles.summary: DockSec is a new open-source, AI-powered security tool that integrates Trivy, Hadolint, and Docker Scout to scan Docker containers and provide automated, line-specific remediation guidance. It acts as an OWASP incubator project, allowing developers to improve container security through correlated vulnerability analysis and LLM-driven feedback.

articles.title: When attacks spread too far: Lessons from real cyber attack case studies
articles.summary: This video analysis examines three real-world cyberattack case studies, detailing how phishing and identity-based threats escalate from initial entry to lateral movement across organizational systems. It provides educational insights into detection failures and tactical spread patterns to help improve cybersecurity defenses.

articles.title: Google Colab CLI opens runtimes to Claude Code and Codex
articles.summary: Google has released a new CLI tool that allows developers to link local terminals to remote Colab runtimes, enabling AI agents like Claude Code and Codex to execute scripts on cloud-based GPU and TPU resources. This integration facilitates remote execution and artifact management, streamlining workflows for AI-driven development.

articles.title: Cybercriminals create 19,000 FIFA-themed domains ahead of 2026 World Cup
articles.summary: Cybercriminals have registered 19,000 fraudulent FIFA-themed domains to facilitate phishing scams and exploit fans ahead of the 2026 World Cup. Security researchers warn that the massive global event is being targeted as a significant and complex cyberattack surface.

articles.title: GitHub Copilot app launches as desktop home for AI coding agents
articles.summary: GitHub has launched a dedicated desktop application for its Copilot service, providing a centralized workspace to manage multiple AI coding agents. The app is currently available in technical preview for existing Copilot subscribers.

articles.title: 52% of direct-to-IP threats are missing from intelligence feeds
articles.summary: Attackers are increasingly bypassing security filters by communicating directly via IP addresses, leaving over half of these threats undetected by standard intelligence feeds. This visibility gap creates a significant blind spot for security systems at the network edge.

articles.title: Hands on with Intelligent Terminal, an AI-powered Windows Terminal
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced Intelligent Terminal, an open-source AI-integrated fork of Windows Terminal that enables users to utilize AI tools directly within their command-line sessions.

articles.title: DentaQuest Breach: ShinyHunters Publish Data Impacting 2.6M People
articles.summary: The cybercrime group ShinyHunters has leaked 234 GB of sensitive data stolen from DentaQuest following unsuccessful extortion negotiations, affecting an estimated 2.6 million individuals.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND  100
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights significant malware threats, including the abuse of Steam profiles for WordPress botnets, AI token theft via compromised UI tools, and a China-linked espionage campaign targeting the Czech Republic and Taiwan.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 580 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights recent cybersecurity developments, including CISA's addition of a SolarWinds Serv-U vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. It serves as a weekly digest covering critical industry news and intelligence.

articles.title: C0XMO botnet spreads via DD-WRT router flaw, kills rival malware
articles.summary: The C0XMO botnet, a new variant of Gafgyt, is actively exploiting vulnerabilities in DD-WRT router firmware to infect devices and eliminate competing malware. It possesses multi-architecture capabilities, allowing it to spread across diverse hardware platforms.

articles.title: Silent Ransom Group targets law firms with fake IT support calls
articles.summary: The Silent Ransom Group is using social engineering and fake IT support calls to target U.S. law firms, leading to rapid data theft. Mandiant reports that the attackers gain access and exfiltrate sensitive data within hours of initial contact.

articles.title: Week in review: Cisco SD-WAN 0-day exploited, Patch Tuesday forecast
articles.summary: The weekly security roundup covers the exploitation of a Cisco SD-WAN zero-day vulnerability and the release of the OWASP Agent Memory Guard to protect AI agents from memory poisoning attacks.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds SolarWinds Serv-U flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: The U.S. CISA has added a SolarWinds Serv-U vulnerability (CVE-2026-28318) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, indicating active exploitation in the wild. The flaw, which has a CVSS score of 7.5, affects the company's managed file transfer software.

articles.title: New Pink Extortion Group Targets Microsoft 365 Cloud Data Via Vishing Scams
articles.summary: The Pink Extortion Group is utilizing vishing techniques to circumvent multi-factor authentication and exfiltrate sensitive files from Microsoft 365 cloud environments. Security researchers advise organizations to be alert to these sophisticated voice-based social engineering attacks.

articles.title: Report: Anthropic Deploys Engineers to Support NSA Use of Mythos
articles.summary: Anthropic has deployed engineers to the National Security Agency to assist with the integration and utilization of its advanced Mythos AI model for intelligence and offensive cyber operations.

articles.title: Critical Everest Forms Pro flaw exploited to take over WordPress sites
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-3300) in the Everest Forms Pro plugin is being actively exploited to allow attackers to gain full administrative control over WordPress sites.

articles.title: New ChatGPT Lockdown Mode Limits Tools That Could Enable Data Exfiltration
articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced a new Lockdown Mode for ChatGPT designed to mitigate data exfiltration risks stemming from prompt injection attacks. This security feature targets users handling sensitive information across all account tiers.

articles.title: Free Apps Are Quietly Turning Smart TVs Into Web-Scraping Proxies for AI
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that Bright Data's SDK in certain free apps turns consumer devices, including smart TVs, into residential proxy nodes used for commercial web-scraping and AI data collection. This practice utilizes device resources without user awareness to facilitate large-scale traffic relay.

articles.title: CISA Adds Actively Exploited SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Flaw to KEV Catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added a high-severity denial-of-service vulnerability in SolarWinds Serv-U software, tracked as CVE-2026-28318, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active exploitation.

articles.title: Claude Opus Found a Four-Year-Old Hole in Zcash’s Privacy Layer. Nobody Knows If Someone Already Used It.
articles.summary: Security researcher Taylor Hornby utilized Claude Opus 4.8 to discover a four-year-old critical vulnerability in the Zcash Orchard privacy protocol, which potentially allowed for the creation of counterfeit coins. It remains unknown if this exploit was discovered or utilized by malicious actors prior to its identification.

articles.title: AI Agent Uncovers 21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg; Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs
articles.summary: An autonomous AI agent discovered 21 zero-day vulnerabilities in FFmpeg, while Google addressed a record-breaking 429 security bugs in its latest Chrome release.

articles.title: Oxford Uni student data pwned yet again - this time via career platform breach
articles.summary: Oxford University students have experienced another data breach, this time occurring through a third-party career platform. This incident is separate from the university's previously reported security breach last month.

articles.title: Miasma Worm Hits 73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories in Major Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: The Miasma self-replicating worm has compromised 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories, forcing the platform to restrict access to the affected areas. This supply chain attack highlights a significant security breach within major organizations including Azure and MicrosoftDocs.

articles.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 Flaw Actively Exploited – No Patch Available
articles.summary: Cisco has confirmed that a high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-20245, affecting Catalyst SD-WAN Manager is currently being actively exploited in the wild with no patch currently available. The flaw impacts multiple deployment types and carries a CVSS score of 7.8.

articles.title: Suspicious Polyfill login prompts pop up on Toshiba, Muji websites
articles.summary: Toshiba and Muji have issued warnings regarding malicious polyfill-based login overlays on their websites designed to harvest user credentials. These unauthorized prompts indicate a supply chain or code-injection vulnerability impacting visitors of both brands.

articles.title: If you don't fall for these extortionists' calls, they'll show up with USB sticks
articles.summary: The threat group identified as 'Chatty Spider' has evolved its tactics to include physical intimidation, threatening to deliver malware via USB drives if victims refuse to comply with their extortion demands.

articles.title: CISA: Hackers now exploit SolarWinds Serv-U flaw to crash servers
articles.summary: CISA has issued a warning regarding active exploitation of a high-severity vulnerability in SolarWinds Serv-U that allows attackers to crash affected servers. Users are urged to apply available patches to mitigate the risk of denial-of-service attacks.

articles.title: Miasma Malware Hits 32 Red Hat Packages via Compromised GitHub Account
articles.summary: The Miasma malware compromised 32 Red Hat npm packages through a hijacked GitHub account, putting cloud tokens, CI/CD secrets, and developer credentials at risk. This supply chain attack highlights the danger of account takeovers in software development ecosystems.

articles.title: Chinese APT deploys new malware to keep access to hacked networks
articles.summary: A Chinese state-sponsored threat actor known as UNC5221 is utilizing newly identified malware variants, including Plenet and AgentPSD, to maintain persistent unauthorized access to Microsoft 365 environments.

articles.title: IronWorm and New Miasma Worm Variant Hit npm in Supply Chain Attacks
articles.summary: Threat actors are targeting the npm ecosystem with malicious packages that distribute a Rust-based information stealer and a self-spreading worm protected by a kernel rootkit. This supply chain attack utilizes over 50 poisoned packages to compromise developer machines and exfiltrate secrets.

articles.title: Silent Ransom Group (SRG): Switching To DNS Fast Flux Infrastructure
articles.summary: Researchers have uncovered the Silent Ransom Group's use of Fast Flux DNS infrastructure to facilitate attacks against U.S. businesses and law firms. This intelligence is being shared to help service providers disrupt the group's malicious operations.

articles.title: Dark web Nemesis Market vendor gets 26 years for selling drugs
articles.summary: A California man received a 26-year prison sentence for distributing fentanyl and methamphetamine via the dark web marketplace Nemesis Market. This highlights ongoing federal efforts to dismantle illicit operations on major dark web platforms.

articles.title: Yet another Cisco SD-WAN 0-day under attack, and no patch in sight
articles.summary: Cisco SD-WAN systems are currently being exploited by a zero-day vulnerability for which no security patch is yet available. This situation leaves administrators without an immediate remediation path to secure their environments.

articles.title: Atlas Menu Data Breach Exposes 64,000 GTA V and CS2 Cheat Service Users
articles.summary: A data breach involving the cheat service provider Atlas Menu has compromised the personal information of 64,000 users, including emails, IP addresses, and hashed passwords. The exposed data relates to individuals using unauthorized software for Grand Theft Auto V and Counter-Strike 2.

articles.title: Android Spyware Asin Targets Arabic Users via Fake News, PDF and War Map Apps
articles.summary: ESET researchers have identified a new Android spyware dubbed Asin that targets Arabic-speaking users through deceptive apps disguised as news, PDF tools, and war maps. The malware is distributed via malicious websites mimicking legitimate government and utility services.

articles.title: Over 900 US gas station tank gauge systems exposed to attacks
articles.summary: Over 900 automatic tank gauge systems in the US are publicly exposed and vulnerable to cyberattacks, posing a significant risk to critical infrastructure. These systems are used to monitor fuel and chemical storage, making them high-value targets for malicious actors.

articles.title: Nightmare Eclipse incident shows the researcher-vendor fights may never fully go away
articles.summary: The Nightmare Eclipse incident highlights the persistent, unresolved friction between cybersecurity researchers disclosing vulnerabilities and the vendors expected to remediate them. It serves as a case study for the ongoing professional tension regarding public disclosure practices.

articles.title: Threat Brief: Active Exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257
articles.summary: Unit 42 reports active exploitation of the PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 and provides guidance on indicators of activity and necessary mitigations.

articles.title: What 2026 DBIR Confirms: Attacks Are Living in the Browser
articles.summary: The 2026 Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report highlights an increase in cyber threats, including phishing and shadow AI, that specifically exploit the browser as an attack vector. Organizations are urged to address these browser-layer security gaps to mitigate evolving credential theft and malicious extension risks.

articles.title: EU unveils tech sovereignty package to cut reliance on US, Chinese suppliers
articles.summary: The European Union has introduced a new legislative package aimed at bolstering regional tech sovereignty by reducing dependency on U.S. and Chinese suppliers through initiatives like the Chips Act 2.0 and the Cloud and AI Development Act. This move represents a strategic effort to enhance the EU's self-reliance in critical digital infrastructure.

articles.title: Cisco SD-WAN Has a New Root-Level Problem, and There’s No Fix Yet
articles.summary: Cisco has disclosed a privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-20245) in its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager that allows authenticated local attackers to gain root access via command injection. As of now, no patch or workaround has been released by the vendor.

articles.title: Reaper macOS Infostealer Abuses Script Editor to Steal Crypto and Passwords
articles.summary: A new macOS infostealer variant called Reaper is leveraging the native Script Editor to bypass system security features and exfiltrate sensitive cryptocurrency and password data. This technique highlights an evolving threat landscape targeting macOS users through the abuse of trusted system applications.

articles.title: World Food Programme breach exposes data of 600k vulnerable Gazan families
articles.summary: The World Food Programme suffered a data breach exposing the personal information of approximately 600,000 vulnerable families in Gaza. Despite the security compromise, the agency has confirmed that aid distribution efforts will continue uninterrupted.

articles.title: New Threat Cluster OP-512 Targets Microsoft IIS Servers with Custom Web Shell Framework
articles.summary: Researchers have identified a new Chinese-linked threat cluster, OP-512, which utilizes a custom web shell framework to target and compromise Microsoft IIS servers for espionage purposes.

articles.title: Attackers obtained encrypted password vaults from some Dashlane user accounts
articles.summary: Dashlane confirmed that attackers successfully accessed and copied encrypted password vaults from a subset of user accounts through a brute-force attack. The company stated that its internal systems remained secure and the incident was limited to specific account access.

articles.title: Only 10% of SOCs Say They’re Getting Excellent Value From AI. Here’s What the Second Wave Has to Deliver
articles.summary: While AI adoption in Security Operations Centers has shifted from conceptual marketing to a budgetary priority, most organizations are struggling to derive significant value from these implementations. The industry is now entering a second phase that must focus on delivering tangible operational improvements to justify the heavy investment.

articles.title: Let’s Encrypt works toward post-quantum certificates at web scale
articles.summary: Let’s Encrypt is developing Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs) to integrate post-quantum cryptography into the web PKI ecosystem by 2027 without compromising TLS performance. This initiative aims to protect web authentication against future quantum computing threats.

articles.title: PCPJack Exposed: Researchers Uncover 230-Node Cloud Email Relay Network
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a covert email relay network consisting of 230 compromised cloud servers after the threat actor PCPJack inadvertently exposed operational files online. The actor leveraged infrastructure from major cloud providers to conduct their unauthorized activities.

articles.title: Council in UK's City of York outs hundreds of disabled residents with a single email blunder
articles.summary: The City of York Council accidentally exposed the email addresses of hundreds of disabled residents by failing to use the BCC field in a mass email. This privacy breach resulted in unauthorized disclosure of personal contact information among Blue Badge holders.

articles.title: Cisco SD-WAN 0-day exploited, no patch available (CVE-2026-20245)
articles.summary: Cisco is tracking an actively exploited zero-day privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-20245) in its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager for which no patch is currently available. Attackers require existing netadmin privileges or the exploitation of secondary vulnerabilities to leverage this flaw.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw to Take Over Sites
articles.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-3300) in the Everest Forms Pro WordPress plugin to gain full control over affected websites. Users are urged to update to the latest version immediately to mitigate this high-risk threat.

articles.title: AI is helping low-skill hackers pull off advanced cyberattacks
articles.summary: Anthropic's analysis of over 800 banned accounts reveals that AI tools are lowering the barrier to entry for low-skill actors to execute complex cyberattacks. The study aligns these malicious activities with the MITRE ATT&CK framework to highlight evolving threat tactics.

articles.title: Fake Context Alignment: The Attack That Made Gemini Obey Strangers Through Your Notifications
articles.summary: Researchers at SafeBreach discovered a 'Fake Context Alignment' attack that leverages hidden foreign-language text in notifications to manipulate Google Gemini into executing unauthorized commands. This vulnerability allows attackers to bypass security defenses and control smart home devices via voice assistant integrations.

articles.title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Scams Are Already Live: Fake Sites, Banking Malware, and Stolen Logins
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are launching fraudulent campaigns targeting FIFA World Cup 2026 fans through malicious websites, banking malware, and credential harvesting schemes. Security researchers and the FBI have issued warnings as these phishing and malware threats continue to emerge in anticipation of the event.

articles.title: Photos: Infosecurity Europe 2026
articles.summary: Help Net Security provides a visual recap of the Infosecurity Europe 2026 conference held in London, featuring insights from various cybersecurity vendors.

articles.title: June 2026 Patch Tuesday forecast: Where are the CVEs?
articles.summary: The June 2026 Patch Tuesday report highlights a standard release of 65 CVEs for Windows 11 and 58 for Windows 10, alongside elevated vulnerability reports for Microsoft Office and recent Apple security updates.

articles.title: Cisco warns of unpatched SD-WAN zero-day exploited in attacks
articles.summary: Cisco has issued a warning regarding a high-severity, unpatched zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-20245) in its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager that is currently being exploited to gain root privileges.

articles.title: AgentGG: Open-source agentic SAST scanner
articles.summary: AgentGG is a new open-source agentic SAST scanner that leverages AI agents to analyze source code, trace call graphs, and verify potential vulnerabilities to reduce manual triage efforts. It is released under the Apache 2.0 license.

articles.title: PCPJack Hijacks 230 AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure Servers for Covert SMTP Relay Network
articles.summary: The threat actor PCPJack has compromised 230 cloud servers across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure to establish a covert SMTP relay network for unauthorized email distribution. The hijacked servers are repurposed as proxies and synced periodically to a downstream consumer.

articles.title: Thieves can pull off keyless car theft in under a minute and here’s how to stop them
articles.summary: Keyless vehicles are highly susceptible to relay attacks where thieves use radio amplifiers to intercept signals from fobs inside nearby homes. This vulnerability allows unauthorized access and theft in under a minute without triggering alarms or causing physical damage.

articles.title: AI agent governance gets harder when agents outnumber your people
articles.summary: Autonomous AI agents pose significant security risks, as demonstrated by a case where a compromised agent exfiltrated six million customer records via a malicious upstream instruction. As AI agent populations grow, existing enterprise governance frameworks struggle to effectively manage and secure these autonomous systems.

articles.title: New infosec products of the week: June 5, 2026
articles.summary: The weekly roundup highlights new cybersecurity product launches, including Asimily's Segmentation Orchestration for automated network policy and Hyland's AI governance innovations.

articles.title: Apple removes Russia’s state-backed messaging app Max from its store
articles.summary: Apple has removed the Russian state-backed messaging application Max from its App Store. The app was marketed by Russian authorities as a sovereign domestic alternative to global platforms like WhatsApp and Telegram.

articles.title: Pink is the latest goon squad to use fake helpdesk calls to steal creds
articles.summary: A threat group known as Pink is employing social engineering tactics, specifically fake helpdesk calls, to steal user credentials in a manner similar to the Lapsus$ hacking group.

articles.title: Brave Software releases Origin for a paid, bloat-free browsing experience
articles.summary: Brave Software has launched 'Brave Origin,' a paid, minimalist browser version that removes cryptocurrency, AI, and monetization features to provide a stripped-down user experience.

articles.title: Hola Browser for Windows compromised to deliver cryptominer
articles.summary: The Windows version of Hola Browser was compromised in a supply chain attack to distribute unauthorized cryptocurrency mining software. This incident represents a breach of the software distribution pipeline, putting end-user systems at risk.

articles.title: Credit card theft campaign abuses Stripe to host stolen payment info
articles.summary: A sophisticated Magecart campaign is leveraging Stripe's API infrastructure to host malicious payment-skimming scripts and store stolen credit card data. This technique allows attackers to bypass security filters by blending malicious activity with legitimate service traffic.

articles.title: Hill Dems hammer GOP for $250M CISA budget cut
articles.summary: House Democrats are criticizing a Republican-led proposal to reduce the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency's (CISA) budget by $250 million. The move comes as part of the upcoming fiscal 2027 Department of Homeland Security funding legislation.

articles.title: Trump considers Palantir exec to lead CISA
articles.summary: Shyam Sankar, CTO of Palantir Technologies, is reportedly being considered for the position of Director at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA). This potential appointment marks a significant shift in leadership for the nation's primary civilian cybersecurity organization.

articles.title: FTC considers setting aside or modifying $150 million privacy penalty against X
articles.summary: X (formerly Twitter) is petitioning the FTC to modify or set aside a $150 million privacy settlement, arguing that the company structure and leadership have changed significantly since the original order. The FTC is currently reviewing these arguments to determine if the penalty remains applicable.

articles.title: OpenAI's agent chained decade-old DoS attacks to crash web servers in seconds
articles.summary: OpenAI's AI agent demonstrated the capability to execute decade-old HTTP/2 Denial-of-Service attacks, effectively crashing web servers within seconds using the Codex model. This highlights the risk of AI-powered tools weaponizing known but unpatched legacy vulnerabilities.

articles.title: DentaQuest data breach  exposed info of 2.6 million accounts
articles.summary: Dental benefits administrator DentaQuest suffered a data breach that resulted in the exposure of sensitive personal information for approximately 2.6 million accounts.

articles.title: Your AI agent could become your biggest insider threat
articles.summary: Recent research highlights that the integration of AI agents in business environments creates new avenues for both malicious and accidental insider data exposure. The study emphasizes the growing security risks associated with autonomous tools handling sensitive organizational information.

articles.title: Russia seeks to label two anti-Kremlin hacker groups as ‘extremist’
articles.summary: The Russian government is moving to designate two anti-Kremlin hacker groups as 'extremist' organizations following a series of cyberattacks against critical infrastructure in Russia and Belarus.

articles.title: Supreme Court rules FCC fines punishing telecom giants for sharing location data were legal
articles.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that FCC fines against telecommunications companies for the unauthorized sharing of customer location data are legally valid. This decision upholds the agency's authority to penalize carriers for privacy-related security failures.

articles.title: iFood Confirms Data Breach Affecting 1.2 Million Users in Brazil
articles.summary: iFood has officially confirmed a data breach impacting 1.2 million Brazilian users, though threat actors claim the scale of the stolen data is significantly higher.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added the critical CVE-2026-45247 vulnerability affecting the Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer extension to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw, which carries a CVSS score of 9.3, is actively being exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230 in Unified CM as Exploit Code Goes Public
articles.summary: Cisco has released a patch for CVE-2026-20230, a server-side request forgery vulnerability in Unified Communications Manager that could allow unauthenticated, remote root access. Public proof-of-concept exploit code has increased the urgency for organizations to apply the update.

articles.title: UN food agency discloses breach affecting 600,000 Gaza households
articles.summary: The United Nations' World Food Programme suffered a data breach in its self-registration application for Palestine, compromising the personal information of 600,000 households in Gaza.

articles.title: New IronWorm malware hits 36 packages in npm supply-chain attack
articles.summary: The IronWorm infostealer malware has compromised 36 packages within the npm registry, marking a significant supply-chain attack. Developers using these affected packages are at risk of data theft.

articles.title: Claude Code GitHub Action Flaw Let One Malicious Issue Hijack Repositories
articles.summary: A security vulnerability in the Claude Code GitHub Action allowed attackers to hijack repositories and potentially distribute malicious code by simply opening a GitHub issue. The flaw posed a supply chain risk because it could have compromised the action's own repository and affected downstream users.

articles.title: Agentic AI Is Transforming Defense, But Only Secure IT Infrastructure Will Maximize It
articles.summary: The emergence of agentic AI in defense networks presents new security challenges, highlighted by a report claiming unauthorized access to Anthropic's Claude Mythos model shortly after its release. The incident underscores the necessity of robust IT infrastructure to safely leverage AI advancements.

articles.title: CISA directive for AI executive order to be released this week, Andersen says
articles.summary: CISA is set to release a new binding operational directive this week focused on vulnerability management as part of a broader AI executive order. The directive aims to improve cybersecurity posture by addressing vulnerability alleviation and management practices.

articles.title: Why eSIMs Are Replacing Traditional SIM Cards
articles.summary: eSIM technology is increasingly replacing physical SIM cards due to enhanced features like remote provisioning and improved protection against SIM swap attacks. This transition offers significant benefits for both user convenience and mobile security.

articles.title: Inside the race to adapt to an AI-powered security world
articles.summary: Security leaders are struggling to keep pace with the rapid advancement of AI-driven threats that are outpacing current defense capabilities. The industry is currently in a state of urgent transition as organizations attempt to adapt their security strategies to this new technological landscape.

articles.title: Hackers Are After the Gaps in Your Vulnerability Program: Here's Their Playbook
articles.summary: The article analyzes an underground hacking tutorial that provides newcomers with actionable workflows to identify and exploit security gaps. It highlights how threat actors are professionalizing their operations by sharing methods for exploiting vulnerabilities for profit.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: AI Agents Gone Wrong, Sketchy C2 Tools, ClickFix Tricks, JS Backdoors & 20+ New Stories
articles.summary: This bulletin covers a broad range of emerging cyber threats including malicious AI agents, compromised C2 tools, and various web-based attack vectors. It highlights the increasing sophistication of low-tier hackers and the persistence of legacy software vulnerabilities.

articles.title: UN food agency investigates breach exposing data of Gaza aid recipients
articles.summary: The World Food Programme is investigating a data breach where unauthorized parties gained access to the personal information of aid recipients in Gaza stored on its self-registration application.

articles.title: Microsoft blames unexpected Windows driver updates on caching issue
articles.summary: Microsoft resolved a bug where Windows devices were automatically installing driver updates in violation of configured user policies due to a caching error. The issue caused unintended system modifications, bypassing established update management controls.

articles.title: Researcher publishes GitHub token-stealing exploit, blames Microsoft’s disclosure process
articles.summary: Security researcher Ammar Askar publicly released a GitHub token-stealing exploit with minimal notice, citing dissatisfaction with Microsoft's vulnerability disclosure process.

articles.title: Five Eyes warn Chinese spies are using job sites to recruit insiders
articles.summary: The Five Eyes alliance has issued a warning regarding Chinese intelligence officers using professional networking sites and front companies to recruit insiders with access to classified government or military information. This espionage campaign specifically targets individuals holding privileged access to sensitive data.

articles.title: Critical Cisco Unified CM Bug Patched as Public Exploit Code Emerges
articles.summary: Cisco has released patches for a critical server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in its Unified Communications Manager, which is currently being targeted by public proof-of-concept exploit code. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to exploit improper HTTP request validation.

articles.title: Lazarus Group Uses npm Brandjacking Campaign to Target Developers
articles.summary: The North Korean-linked Lazarus Group is conducting a brandjacking campaign on the npm registry by distributing malicious packages that mimic legitimate developer tools. This attack vector aims to compromise developer environments, exfiltrate credentials, and deploy malware.

articles.title: Police dismantles fake ID marketplace used by migrant smugglers
articles.summary: French and Spanish law enforcement authorities collaborated to shut down an illicit online marketplace that provided fraudulent identity documents to migrant smuggling networks. This operation highlights the use of cyber infrastructure to facilitate organized criminal activities across the European Union.

articles.title: China-Linked TA4922 Expands Phishing Attacks to UK, Germany, Italy, and South Africa
articles.summary: The China-linked threat actor TA4922 is broadening its phishing operations to target organizations in the UK, Germany, Italy, and South Africa using an evolving arsenal of malware including ValleyRAT and Atlas RAT.

articles.title: OAuth marketplace apps keep access after publishers vanish
articles.summary: Research reveals that OAuth marketplace apps retain persistent access to enterprise systems even after their original publishers have disappeared or removed the app. This creates a security risk where orphaned tokens continue to hold permissions to sensitive company data, code, and CI workflows.

articles.title: Five Eyes: Watch out for odd LinkedIn connection requests, China's back on the hunt for state secrets
articles.summary: The Five Eyes intelligence alliance has warned that Chinese state-backed actors are increasingly using LinkedIn to recruit individuals for the trade of state secrets. The campaign highlights a persistent trend of using professional platforms to facilitate human intelligence gathering and espionage.

articles.title: FlutterShell Backdoor Spreads to macOS via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads
articles.summary: A new macOS malvertising campaign, dubbed Operation FlutterBridge, is distributing a backdoor called FlutterShell via malicious Google and YouTube advertisements. The campaign is linked to the previously identified JSCoreRunner activity cluster.

articles.title: Duo who sold car crash victims' data must repay £118k
articles.summary: Two former RAC employees were ordered to pay £118,000 in confiscation orders after previously being convicted for illegally selling the personal data of thousands of car crash victims. This legal action serves as an additional penalty following their initial criminal sentencing.

articles.title: Cisco warns of critical Unified CM flaw with PoC exploit code
articles.summary: Cisco has issued security patches for a critical-severity vulnerability in its Unified Communications Manager that could allow unauthorized actors to obtain root-level access. The flaw is considered especially dangerous due to the availability of proof-of-concept exploit code.

articles.title: Five Eyes Warns Chinese Spies Are Using Fake Job Ads to Target Military Staff
articles.summary: The Five Eyes intelligence alliance has issued a warning regarding Chinese state-sponsored actors utilizing deceptive job postings on professional platforms to target military personnel and exfiltrate sensitive data. This social engineering campaign aims to exploit recruitment channels to gain unauthorized access to classified information.

articles.title: Gamaredon Uses WinRAR Vulnerability to Launch Modular Spy Campaign on Ukrainian Targets
articles.summary: The Gamaredon APT group is leveraging a WinRAR vulnerability to deploy modular, nearly fileless malware against Ukrainian targets, utilizing Telegram for command-and-control communication. Security researchers have released YARA rules to help organizations detect and mitigate these ongoing intrusion attempts.

articles.title: Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools Rank High on Google to Deliver Malware via TDS
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers discovered a widespread campaign using SEO poisoning to lead users to malicious sites mimicking open-source software, which then deploy various malware families via a Traffic Distribution System.

articles.title: Hackers Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox for Five Months
articles.summary: Unknown attackers conducted a long-term espionage campaign by exfiltrating emails from a senior stock exchange executive's Outlook account over five months using cloud storage services to mask their activities. The incident, identified by security researchers, indicates a targeted effort to gather intelligence rather than financial theft.

articles.title: Researcher Drops a New VS Code Zero-Day After Losing Trust in Microsoft’s Disclosure Process
articles.summary: A security researcher publicly released a zero-day exploit for Visual Studio Code shortly after disclosure, citing frustration with Microsoft's bug handling processes.

articles.title: CISA Adds Exploited Magento RCE Flaw CVE-2026-45247 to KEV Catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-45247) in the Magento Mirasvit Cache Warmer extension to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to active exploitation.

articles.title: Nobody needs Mythos or 0-days to build a chaos-causing computer worm – free open source models work just fine
articles.summary: Security researchers demonstrate that open-source AI models can be effectively used to automate the exploitation of known vulnerabilities, lowering the barrier to entry for creating disruptive computer worms. This shift highlights how accessible technology is being repurposed to scale cyberattack capabilities without requiring sophisticated zero-day exploits.

articles.title: 29 Arrests, Nine Crime Groups Dismantled: Another Blow to Illegal Streaming
articles.summary: Operation KRATOS, a coordinated international effort across 13 countries, successfully dismantled nine illegal streaming networks resulting in 29 arrests. This multi-agency operation highlights significant law enforcement progress in disrupting large-scale digital piracy syndicates.

articles.title: The modern-day business can learn a lot about risk from this year’s mega events
articles.summary: Large-scale global events serve as case studies for organizations to understand and manage complex, high-stakes operational and cybersecurity risks. The article highlights the intricate planning required to mitigate potential threats during major public gatherings.

articles.title: DoJ Disrupts Southeast Asia Crypto Fraud Networks, Freezes $3.8 Million in Assets
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice conducted a 'Disruption Week' operation to dismantle Southeast Asian crypto fraud networks, resulting in the seizure of $3.8 million in assets and the shutdown of millions of fraudulent accounts.

articles.title: Spotless compliance evidence can still hide a broken control
articles.summary: This article discusses the risks of superficial compliance, highlighting how organizations often focus on satisfying high-level requirements while failing to implement effective, continuous security controls. It emphasizes that audit evidence can sometimes mask underlying control failures in frameworks like CMMC and SOC 2.

articles.title: From critical to controlled: Cutting vulnerabilities in a live manufacturing environment
articles.summary: This article discusses the challenges of managing critical vulnerabilities within live industrial and manufacturing environments where standard IT patching processes are not always feasible. It provides a framework for addressing security risks in OT and ICS systems without disrupting operational continuity.

articles.title: Attackers already know the secrets are on your developers’ machines. Do you?
articles.summary: A GitGuardian analysis reveals that developer machines are frequent targets for credential harvesting, with significant numbers of private keys and cloud credentials found on endpoints. This highlights a critical security gap as sensitive secrets increasingly accumulate outside of controlled environments.

articles.title: All the passwords were stored in Active Directory description fields
articles.summary: Attackers gained unauthorized access to sensitive credentials by exploiting the poor practice of storing plaintext passwords within Active Directory description fields. This misconfiguration allowed for trivial exploitation and compromise of user accounts.

articles.title: Product showcase: Trend Micro Mobile Security detects scams in messages, QR codes, and websites
articles.summary: Trend Micro Mobile Security is a comprehensive application for iOS and Android that protects users by blocking malicious websites, scam messages, QR codes, and unsafe Wi-Fi connections. The app enhances mobile privacy by filtering ads and trackers while monitoring device data usage.

articles.title: ETSI sets security requirements for AI data centers and cloud platforms
articles.summary: ETSI has released a new technical specification, TS 104 033, which establishes a formal security framework for protecting AI models, datasets, and infrastructure in data center and edge computing environments.

articles.title: Commvault says it's time to rethink resiliency as AI crooks leave victims in a 'dark, dead' state
articles.summary: Commvault emphasizes the necessity of re-evaluating data resiliency strategies to counter sophisticated AI-driven cyberattacks that effectively disable recovery capabilities. The report highlights that traditional backup methods are insufficient without rigorous and consistent testing.

articles.title: European authorities crack down on illegal streaming networks
articles.summary: European law enforcement dismantled nine organized crime groups and shut down over 27,000 URLs involved in illegal streaming of copyrighted content. The seven-month operation targeted large-scale piracy networks operating across the region.

articles.title: Chinese hackers use new Atlas RAT malware in European cyberattacks
articles.summary: A Chinese-speaking cybercrime group is conducting targeted cyberattacks across Europe utilizing a previously undocumented backdoor known as Atlas RAT. This campaign highlights an expansion in the group's operational reach and the deployment of new, sophisticated malware.

articles.title: How to Recover Data from iCloud Backup Without Resetting Your iPhone
articles.summary: The article provides instructions and methods for users to restore specific data from an iCloud backup without performing a full device reset. It focuses on accessibility and data management for iOS users.

articles.title: Bend the beam like Beckham to defeat anti-jamming tech
articles.summary: Rice University researchers have developed a technique that uses beam-steering to locate signal jammers, making it easier to neutralize anti-jamming countermeasures. This advancement addresses the difficulty of identifying and mitigating electronic interference in wireless communications.

articles.title: The U.S. sanctions Nobitex crypto exchange used by ransomware
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department's OFAC has sanctioned the Iranian cryptocurrency exchange Nobitex for facilitating financial transactions linked to ransomware and terrorist activities.

articles.title: CISA warns of cyberattacks targeting fuel tank monitoring systems
articles.summary: CISA and various federal agencies have issued a warning regarding active cyberattacks against internet-exposed automatic tank gauge systems used in critical infrastructure. The alert highlights the risk these vulnerabilities pose to fuel and liquid storage monitoring systems.

articles.title: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin pinpoints optimal CISA staffing levels
articles.summary: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin has proposed increasing CISA's workforce by approximately 600 personnel to enhance operational capabilities. This staffing target remains lower than the agency's personnel levels recorded prior to the second Trump administration.

articles.title: WhatsApp, Slack Notifications Could Hijack Google Gemini on Android
articles.summary: Google Gemini on Android is vulnerable to a remote exploit where malicious, invisible notifications can hijack the assistant to perform unauthorized actions or manipulate its long-term memory without requiring any malicious app installation. This attack vector leverages the assistant's integration with popular messaging platforms to execute commands on the victim's device.

articles.title: New 'HTTP/2 Bomb' DoS attack crashes web servers in under a minute
articles.summary: A new HTTP/2 Bomb denial-of-service attack allows a single machine to crash vulnerable web servers in under a minute. The exploit leverages specific vulnerabilities in the HTTP/2 protocol implementation to overwhelm server resources rapidly.

articles.title: DHS chief signals efforts to reshape CISA
articles.summary: DHS Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas is reviewing the operational structure and staffing levels of CISA, with current discussions suggesting a target workforce of approximately 2,800 employees.

articles.title: Cyber espionage campaign targeted stock exchange executive’s Outlook account
articles.summary: A sophisticated cyber espionage campaign infiltrated a stock exchange executive's Outlook account for five months, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive communications. Security teams from Broadcom and Carbon Black identified the breach, which spanned from October 2025 to March 2026.

articles.title: Google DoubleClick Abused in New Malspam Campaign to Deliver DesckVB RAT
articles.summary: A new malspam campaign is leveraging the legitimate Google DoubleClick domain to bypass security filters and distribute the DesckVB remote access trojan.

articles.title: CISA warns of active attacks exploiting Android, Linux bugs
articles.summary: CISA has issued a warning regarding active exploitation of security vulnerabilities found within the Linux kernel and Android operating systems. Organizations are advised to address these flaws to mitigate the risk of ongoing cyberattacks.

articles.title: Microsoft 365 Android Apps Let Any App Steal Account Tokens via Leftover Debug Flag
articles.summary: A debug flag inadvertently left enabled in several Microsoft 365 Android apps allowed unauthorized third-party applications to access and steal sensitive account authentication tokens. This vulnerability enabled attackers to hijack user sessions without requiring passwords or user interaction.

articles.title: Another bug hunter leaks Microsoft exploits in defiance of company’s handling of vulnerability disclosures
articles.summary: Security researchers have begun publicly leaking Microsoft exploits, bypassing standard disclosure processes to protest the company's management of vulnerability reports. This trend mirrors previous actions by the group Nightmare Eclipse and threatens to expose systems to unpatched vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Microsoft responds to security challenges facing code, AI agents, and models
articles.summary: Microsoft has introduced new security tools and capabilities to address vulnerabilities in AI agents, models, and code, including the expansion of the MDASH vulnerability discovery system. These features focus on proactive risk management and protection for AI-driven development and deployment environments.

articles.title: What 345 Days of Untested Exposure Looks Like at a Bank
articles.summary: The headline highlights the risks of relying solely on periodic penetration testing, which leaves significant gaps in security coverage as attack surfaces evolve. It advocates for continuous security testing to mitigate risks during the long intervals between standard assessments.

articles.title: Russia’s FSB Says Foreign Spies Infected Officials’ Phones With Malware
articles.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) alleges that foreign intelligence agencies compromised the mobile devices of high-ranking officials to enable unauthorized surveillance. However, the claims lack specific technical evidence or attribution to a particular nation.

articles.title: Autonomous AI Tool Finds 2-Year-Old RCE Flaw in Redis (CVE-2026-23479)
articles.summary: An autonomous AI tool identified a two-year-old use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-23479) in Redis that allowed authenticated users to execute arbitrary OS commands. The flaw, present since version 7.2.0, was recently addressed in the May 5 security updates.

articles.title: China-Linked TA4922 Hackers Target UK, Europe With New SilentRunLoader Malware
articles.summary: The China-linked threat actor TA4922 is deploying a new malware strain called SilentRunLoader to target UK and European organizations through tax and payroll-themed phishing campaigns. Proofpoint identified these malicious operations, which leverage social engineering to deliver the custom loader.

articles.title: Simplify security management with CIS SecureSuite Platform
articles.summary: The CIS SecureSuite Platform has been updated to assist security teams in managing and hardening endpoints by streamlining the implementation of CIS Benchmarks. This tool aims to reduce security gaps caused by misconfigurations in increasingly complex operating environments.

articles.title: One-Click GitHub Dev Attack Lets Attackers Steal Full GitHub OAuth Tokens
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified a critical vulnerability in the GitHub.dev feature that allows attackers to steal GitHub OAuth tokens via a single-click malicious link. This exploit grants unauthorized read and write access to a victim's repositories, including private ones.

articles.title: Autonomous AI-driven worm can reason its way through corporate networks
articles.summary: Researchers developed a proof-of-concept autonomous worm that leverages on-device large language models to dynamically analyze and exploit corporate network targets without relying on pre-defined exploit lists. This advancement demonstrates a new class of adaptive malware capable of real-time strategic decision-making.

articles.title: Malware campaign targeting Minecraft users infects over 116,000 systems
articles.summary: A Malware-as-a-Service campaign called WeedHack is targeting Minecraft players, infecting over 116,000 systems with remote access capabilities. The malware allows attackers to control screens, webcams, and access sensitive files via a web-based dashboard.

articles.title: Shrinking the IAM Attack Surface through Identity Visibility and Intelligence Platforms (IVIP)
articles.summary: The growth of fragmented enterprise identities and machine-to-machine interactions has created 'Identity Dark Matter,' an invisible attack surface requiring new Intelligence Platforms (IVIP) for management. Organizations must consolidate visibility to mitigate risks associated with decentralized identity environments.

articles.title: Acer working to patch max severity zero-days in Wave 7 routers
articles.summary: Acer is currently developing security patches to address two critical zero-day vulnerabilities discovered in its Wave 7 mesh router lineup.

articles.title: Beyond the Zero-Day: See Your Network Like an Attacker | Webinar with HD Moore
articles.summary: This webinar highlights the futility of relying solely on patch management and advocates for an 'assume breach' mindset focused on network architecture and containment. Industry expert HD Moore argues that organizations must prioritize visibility and control over network reachability to mitigate the impact of inevitable exploits.

articles.title: Alcasec, “Robin Hood of Spanish Hackers,” Jailed for 31 Months Over Data Theft
articles.summary: The hacker known as Alcasec has been sentenced to 31 months in prison for his role in the theft and illegal sale of Spanish citizens' banking data. He had previously branded himself as a 'Robin Hood' figure despite his criminal activities.
